sara_arch: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — I want to propose a simple cohesion x customer-impact prioritization matrix to sequence service carveouts and tech-debt paydown. TL;DR: extract high-cohesion, high-impact units first.

matt_backend: +1. makes sense. can you paste the matrix so we all have the same mental model?

sara_arch: sure — rough matrix (for discussion):
```
High cohesion + High impact  -> extract early (low risk, high ROI)
Low cohesion  + High impact  -> stabilize interface + adapter (medium)
High cohesion + Low impact   -> schedule later, bundle with other low-impact work
Low cohesion  + Low impact   -> deprioritize / archive / re-evaluate
```

jenna_pm: timeline and customer surface? which user flows qualify as "high impact" here?

omar_infra: infra note: some extractions will force changes to GPU pooling and tenancy assumptions. we should flag ops-heavy ones as medium priority until we have a staging pattern.

li_research: also flag model-runtime compatibility — anything touching KV cache or quantized paths needs a compatibility shim. otherwise we'll see perf surprises in prod.

annie_sre: rollout guardrails: per-route tracing, cost/latency dashboards, and a regression alert baseline. recommend canary traffic + automated rollback on 3% latency or 1% error regression.

matt_backend: migration pattern proposal: keep a facade in front of the new service, proxy by route, and flip traffic incrementally. example routes snippet: 
```
# routes.yaml
- path: /session/*
  handler: session-facade
  fallback: runtime/session
```
This lets us run the new service behind the facade and route small % initially.

deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled: canary-2028-03-18 -> started :rocket:

jenna_pm: OK — proposed priorities (based on product impact + technical tractability):
1) Session-auth/identity extract (owner: matt_backend) — Q3 target
2) KV-cache ownership split (owner: li_research + sara_arch) — Q4 target
3) Model-profile registry decouple (owner: sara_arch) — Q1 next year
Owners can push/pull as needed but want these on the roadmap.

sara_arch: I agree with that ordering. I'll open the epics and add acceptance criteria (backwards-compatible API, perf parity within 10%, feature-flagged).

matt_backend: taking lead on session-auth. will draft API contract PR by EOW and add migration tests.

annie_sre: I'll prepare SLO templates and runbooks for the canary/rollback steps. will require a short playbook for oncall.

li_research: I'll create perf bench harness for the new paths (KV + quantization). will run baseline and attach numbers to the RFC.

sara_arch: thanks. action items: 1) matt — API PR + epic, 2) li — perf harness, 3) annie — SLO/runbooks, 4) myself — epics + RFC update. I'll update the schedule in the deck and drop a link.

matt_backend: quick Q — do we want a separate repo for some of these extracts or keep mono with a carveout directory? ops prefers separate services for independent deploys.

omar_infra: separate repos make infra automation easier, but we should standardize build + image templates first. I'll add infra checklist to the epic.

sara_arch: noted. last thing: let's not aim for perfect decomposition in first pass. prefer small, testable slices with clear rollback paths. :heavy_check_mark:

sara_arch: RFC link (will update after I file epics): https://r.wdm/rfc/cohesion-matrix

jenna_pm: thanks all — will sync in next PM/eng sync. any objections to the priorities?

matt_backend: none from me.

li_research: good to go.

annie_sre: good. i'll start runbooks.

sara_arch: closing thread — I'll post epics and assign tickets shortly. appreciate the quick alignment. :pray:
